title: The Doctor Who Transcripts - The Deadly Assassin

rooms.name: TARDIS - Wooden Console Room
rooms.description: The Doctor's TARDIS interior, specifically an older-style console room with wooden panelling and a built-in writing desk. It is dimly lit at times, with a viewscreen used to observe outside events on Gallifrey. The space is used for planning, hiding, and quick improvisation as the Doctor prepares to warn the Time Lord President. The room also becomes the site of a disturbing precognitive vision of the Panopticon assassination.
items: Doctor's coat and scarf (used as decoy)
events: Doctor has vision of the Panopticon and the President being shot
Doctor writes warning note to the Castellan
Guards unlock and enter but are fooled by a decoy
Doctor monitors Panopticon broadcast on viewscreen

rooms.name: TARDIS - Interior Rooms (Storage/Side Room)
rooms.description: A secondary interior area of the TARDIS accessed from the console room, used for storage and quick access to travel gear. The Doctor retrieves a Gladstone bag and a hookah pipe from here, suggesting a cluttered, lived-in space. It functions as a practical staging area for disguises and supplies. The room is only briefly seen but clearly distinct from the main console room.
events: Doctor gathers items before attempting to slip past Gallifreyan guards

rooms.name: Gallifrey - Sector 7 (Capitol Perimeter / Cloisters Zone)
rooms.description: A guarded exterior zone on Gallifrey at the perimeter of the Capitol, identified as Sector Seven and associated with cloisters. It is an unauthorized capsule-entry area monitored by tannoy alerts and patrolled by Chancery Guards. The TARDIS materializes here, immediately triggering a security response and a search operation. The area includes access to a communications tower and a lift system used by guards and intruders.
events: TARDIS materializes and is surrounded
Guards attempt entry using keys
Doctor escapes toward tower and a guard is shot by a shadowy figure
Search ordered across the tower’s floors
TARDIS is later transducted away to the Museum

rooms.name: Communications Tower - Lift (Sector 7)
rooms.description: A lift serving the communications tower in Sector Seven, used by guards to move between floors quickly. The Doctor summons it during his escape attempt, only to find it occupied by a guard. A shadowy figure shoots the escorting guard, creating confusion that allows the Doctor to slip away. The lift becomes a focal point of the manhunt as guards assume the Doctor entered the tower.
events: Doctor attempts to use lift to escape
Guard escort is killed by a shadowy figure
Doctor rides and exits quickly, then hides while guards respond

rooms.name: Communications Tower - Floors (Sector 7)
rooms.description: The interior floors of the communications tower, described as a building of roughly fifty-three stories. Guards conduct a floor-by-floor search after believing the Doctor has entered. The search ultimately finds nothing, implying the Doctor doubled back rather than remaining inside. The tower functions mainly as a decoy location that drains security resources.
events: Manhunt ordered to check every floor
Search concludes the Doctor never left the lift and likely doubled back

rooms.name: Records Room (Capitol Archives / Data Retrieval)
rooms.description: A secure archival and computing space where Time Lord data extracts are retrieved and analyzed. It contains consoles, data tubes, operating keys, and the APC (Amplified Panatropic Computations) interface used to access the Matrix. Spandrell and Engin use the room to investigate the Doctor’s status, the missing registration imbalance, and later the Master’s erased records. The room becomes a crisis site when Solis attempts sabotage and when the APC circuits begin to smoke and fail.
events: Type 40 registration imbalance discovered
Doctor’s banishment record and CIA addendum revealed
Debate over whether a DE was withdrawn and how records could be erased
Doctor enters the Matrix via APC
Solis attempts to interfere with APC controls and is shot
APC overload threatens destruction of stored brain patterns
Post-crisis analysis of the Master’s supposed death and poison needle

rooms.name: Chancellery (High Council Offices)
rooms.description: A formal political chamber where Chancellor Goth and Cardinal Borusa conduct high-level discussions and issue orders. It is furnished with imposing seating, including a fur-covered chair and later a dust-covered desk after the catastrophe. Decisions here drive the rapid trial, the election timetable, and the manipulation of public narrative. The Chancellery also becomes the place where Spandrell assigns covert tasks and where the Doctor is finally dismissed from Gallifrey.
items: official documents (resignation honours list referenced elsewhere)
events: Spandrell briefs Goth about the Doctor and requests guards
Goth insists on immediate trial and execution timetable
Borusa and Goth argue over tradition vs crisis
Borusa orders the truth to be 'adjusted' and the Master’s corpse cosmetically altered
After the disaster, Borusa blames devastation and orders the Doctor to leave

rooms.name: Capitol Museum
rooms.description: A museum space within the Time Lord Capitol where artifacts and regalia are displayed on plinths and in cases. The TARDIS is transducted here and placed on a plinth, allowing the Doctor to emerge inside the Capitol. The Doctor uses the museum’s displays to improvise a disguise by taking ceremonial clothing. Spandrell’s team later uses a tracker to trace the Doctor’s path from the TARDIS to the regalia display.
exits: TARDIS - Wooden Console Room (via TARDIS doors)
items: Time Lord regalia display (gold robe and headdress)
long case clock (later conceals the Master’s escape)
events: TARDIS transducted into museum
Doctor steals/uses regalia for disguise
Tracker traces Doctor’s movements
Final departure: Doctor returns to TARDIS and dematerialises
Master’s presence revealed via long case clock which dematerialises

rooms.name: Adytum (Master’s Hidden Chamber)
rooms.description: A concealed, private chamber used by the Master and his agents to observe and direct events within the Capitol. It contains a couch and later a red metal helmet interface showing an eye-view feed from within the Matrix. The Master issues orders here, including conditioning Solis to sabotage the Doctor’s Matrix attempt. The Master and Goth later return here after the Matrix struggle, where the Master berates Goth and attempts a final gambit.
items: chair where the Master sits feigning death
events: Master predicts Doctor’s movements and orders rapid death
Helmet feed shows Matrix pursuit
Solis is conditioned to obey only the Master
After Matrix failure, Master removes helmet from Goth and attempts to trap the Doctor
Needle evidence is later recovered from under the chair

rooms.name: Time Lords Robing Room
rooms.description: A preparation room where Time Lords change into ceremonial robes before entering the Panopticon. It is busy and conversational, with gowns hung on hooks and attendants moving garments around. The Doctor infiltrates the room in a plain shirt and assists a Time Lord into gold robes, enabling his own disguise and access. The room highlights the complacency of the establishment just before violence erupts.
events: Doctor swaps/handles robes to facilitate disguise
Time Lords notice missing or incorrect gowns

rooms.name: Panopticon (Main Chamber)
rooms.description: The grand ceremonial hall of the Time Lords, arranged around a circular central dais with galleries above. It hosts the President’s resignation ceremony, the assassination, and later the trial proceedings. A rear panel transforms into steps for the President’s entrance, and the dais becomes the focal point of both pageantry and catastrophe. After the Master’s later sabotage, the Panopticon shakes and partially collapses as the Eye of Harmony is exposed beneath the floor.
items: chalk outline of the President’s body
display case of relics (includes Great Key/Rod)
floor aperture to Eye of Harmony mechanism
events: Time Lords gather for resignation ceremony
Doctor rushes to gallery and fires, President falls
Doctor is arrested and trial is convened/adjourned here
Investigation of camera evidence begins
Master steals the Great Key and opens the dais to reveal the Eye of Harmony
Doctor replaces pipes/valves to stop catastrophe; Master falls into a chasm

rooms.name: Panopticon Gallery
rooms.description: An elevated viewing gallery overlooking the Panopticon dais, used by media and security vantage points. It contains the Public Register camera position and railings where a weapon is assembled and placed. The Doctor enters here to confront the assassination attempt and later returns during the investigation, where Runcible discovers the condensed remains of his technician inside the camera tube. The gallery is repeatedly used by the Master’s agents to manipulate evidence and kill witnesses.
events: Cameraman/technician is attacked and later found dead via matter condensation
Weapon is positioned to frame the Doctor
Doctor shoots from gallery during assassination moment
Assassin removes discs from recording drum
Runcible is later killed (stake in back) after leaving the gallery sequence

rooms.name: Panopticon Antechamber
rooms.description: A formal waiting area adjacent to the Panopticon where the President prepares to enter the ceremony. The Gold Usher checks the President’s items, including the resignation honours list, and presents the Rod of Office. It serves as a controlled threshold between private preparation and public ritual. The scene underscores how close the assassination threat is to the heart of the ceremony.
events: Final preparations before the President enters the Panopticon

rooms.name: Detention Room (Capitol Holding Cage)
rooms.description: A harsh security chamber designed for high-risk prisoners, featuring a cage atop a pillar reached by a retractable walkway. Entry requires passing through a weapons detector, emphasizing containment and control. The Doctor is chained with his hands above his head and subjected to coercive interrogation. The room embodies the Time Lords’ capacity for brutality when politically pressured.
events: Doctor is tortured for confession
Spandrell halts the torture and questions motive and timeline
Doctor explains he believes he is being framed

rooms.name: Capitol Corridor (Evidence Demonstration Corridor)
rooms.description: A corridor within the Capitol used by Spandrell and the Doctor to test the rifle’s fixed sights. A symbol at the far end becomes the target for a demonstration shot, proving the weapon cannot accurately hit what it appears to aim at. The corridor functions as an investigative space rather than a transit-only area. It marks a turning point where Spandrell begins to accept the Doctor’s framing claim.
events: Spandrell fires and misses, confirming sights are fixed
Doctor argues the real assassin was among the High Council
Decision made to retrieve Public Register camera evidence

rooms.name: Service Ducts and Foundations (Below Records Room)
rooms.description: A deep understructure beneath the Records Room, consisting of service ducts and much older vaults and foundations. Engin describes it as extending a long way down, dating from ancient times. The Doctor suspects a hidden Matrix tap-in might be routed through these lower levels. Although not fully explored on-screen, it is explicitly identified as a distinct sub-level beneath the archives.
exits: Panopticon Vault (via older structures, implied connection)
events: Doctor requests to be shown what lies beneath the Records Room while tracing Goth’s Matrix link

rooms.name: Panopticon Vault
rooms.description: A sealed mortuary vault beneath or adjacent to the Panopticon, used to store bodies and ceremonial dead. It contains biers holding the President, Goth, and the Master’s corpse-like body, and later becomes the site of the Master’s resurrection ruse and escape. The Master seals the entrance, trapping the Doctor and allies while he proceeds with his plan above. An old sloping service shaft provides a difficult escape route back up to the Panopticon.
exits: Capitol Interior Routes (vault door, when unsealed)
events: Bodies stored after assassination and aftermath
Master awakens and shrinks Hildred into a doll
Master shoots Spandrell and the Doctor, forces Engin to hand over the Sash
Vault door sealed, forcing escape via service shaft while Panopticon destabilizes

rooms.name: Panopticon - Eye of Harmony Chamber (Under-Dais Mechanism)
rooms.description: A hidden chamber accessed by opening a section of the Panopticon dais using the Great Key/Rod. Inside is the Eye of Harmony manifested as a bright, crystalline monolith connected to multiple pipes with red valve handles. The Master removes pipes to destabilize the system, causing violent tremors and structural collapse across the Capitol. The Doctor restores the connections, re-stabilizing the Eye and preventing obliteration of the stellar system.
events: Master opens the dais and reveals the Eye of Harmony
Pipes are removed and the Capitol begins to collapse
Doctor fights the Master and replaces pipes to stop the catastrophe
Master falls into a chasm as the floor splits

rooms.name: Matrix - Betchworth Quarry
rooms.description: A simulated chalk quarry environment within the Matrix, identified as Betchworth quarry. It features loose chalk slopes, precipices, sparse shrubs, and a nearby stream with an alligator, all presented as lethal hazards. The Doctor is attacked by surreal intrusions, including a samurai who cuts his scarf, sending him tumbling. Later, the quarry visually transforms into circuit boards as the Doctor asserts the artificial nature of the environment.
exits: Matrix - Quarry Valley and Cliff Face
events: Doctor arrives in quarry and is attacked by samurai illusion
Doctor denies reality and quarry morphs into circuitry
Eyes appear in quarry wall as the Master asserts control

rooms.name: Matrix - Operating Theatre
rooms.description: A stark medical operating theatre illusion with a bright overhead surgical light and a masked surgeon poised with a large syringe. The surgeon wears opaque round spectacles, concealing identity and heightening menace. The Master speaks here, claiming dominion over the Doctor in the Matrix. The Doctor escapes by rolling away, triggering a rapid transition into other combat environments.
events: Master confronts Doctor in surgical guise and attempts injection
Doctor evades and falls into the next illusion

rooms.name: Matrix - World War One Battlefield
rooms.description: A chaotic battlefield illusion resembling World War One, filled with explosions and the sense of imminent death. The environment is designed to overwhelm the Doctor with fear and adrenaline. It functions as a transitional combat zone rather than a place to hide or reason. The Doctor runs through it before the Matrix shifts again.
events: Doctor drops into battlefield and flees amid explosions

rooms.name: Matrix - Railway Tracks Junction
rooms.description: A railway intersection illusion with multiple tracks, moving points, and several engines nearby. The drivers’ faces are concealed, adding to the uncanny threat. The Doctor’s foot is trapped between rails as the points shift, and an oncoming train bears down with a whistle. He survives by throwing himself aside and later frees his foot, recognizing the scenario as an illusion.
events: Doctor’s foot is trapped by moving points
Train nearly strikes him; he escapes and rejects the illusion

rooms.name: Matrix - Quarry Valley and Cliff Face (Hunter Pursuit Zone)
rooms.description: A broader quarry pursuit area connected to the chalk cliffs, including a valley approach route used by the hunter. The Doctor hides on a cliff face behind a buddleia bush, unaware of a giant spider in its web nearby. The hunter stalks methodically, consulting a map and focusing on the Doctor’s need for water. This zone emphasizes pursuit tactics and environmental traps rather than sudden set-piece transitions.
items: hunter’s rifle fire impacts on chalk cliff
events: Hunter fires repeatedly and misses
Doctor hides near spider web
Hunter identifies Doctor’s need for water and moves to exploit it

rooms.name: Matrix - Lightly Wooded Slope (Biplane Attack)
rooms.description: A lightly wooded area reached by descending from the quarry, where the Doctor is attacked from above by a circling biplane. The plane dives low, buzzes him, and returns for strafing runs, forcing the Doctor to flee in terror. The Doctor’s leg appears to bleed, then the injury vanishes and returns, demonstrating the Master’s control over psychosomatic effects. The setting blends natural cover with aerial threat, keeping the Doctor moving.
exits: Matrix - Quarry Valley and Cliff Face
events: Biplane performs multiple attack runs
Doctor’s bleeding injury appears and disappears as he denies it

rooms.name: Matrix - Reed Thicket (Water Trap Area)
rooms.description: A dense reed thicket near a water source where the hunter contaminates the pool with a green liquid. The hunter retreats into the reeds to conceal his actions, setting a trap for the Doctor’s thirst. The Doctor later uses reeds both as tools and as cover, moving between concealment and the water’s edge. The thicket’s density makes visibility poor and ambush likely.
exits: Matrix - Quarry Valley and Cliff Face
events: Hunter poisons the water and hides in reeds
Doctor observes suspicious activity and investigates

rooms.name: Matrix - Poisoned Pool
rooms.description: A pool that appears to offer relief but is deliberately poisoned by the hunter. The Doctor stops himself from drinking, finds the discarded bottle, and confirms contamination by smell. He improvises a reed straw to draw safer water from the margins, demonstrating adaptation under pressure. The pool becomes a tactical pivot point where the Doctor turns the hunter’s trap into an opportunity.
exits: Matrix - Thicket and Tree Ambush Zone
events: Doctor avoids poisoned water and drinks safely using reed straw
Doctor withdraws as hunter closes in

rooms.name: Matrix - Thicket and Tree Ambush Zone
rooms.description: A mixed thicket and tree area where the Doctor sets an ambush using a poisoned thorn as a blowpipe dart. He pricks himself on thorns while moving through cover, then climbs a tree to gain position. The hunter approaches cautiously, is struck in the thigh, and fires back, wounding the Doctor’s upper arm. The zone emphasizes improvised weaponry and close-range cat-and-mouse tactics.
events: Doctor poisons thorn and shoots hunter
Hunter shoots Doctor in the arm
Hunter administers antidote and continues pursuit

rooms.name: Matrix - Marsh (Marsh Gas Battleground)
rooms.description: A marshy landscape with unstable footing and pockets of marsh gas, forcing the Doctor to use a branch as a walking aid. The environment is physically exhausting and amplifies the Doctor’s weakening condition. It becomes the final confrontation site where Goth reveals himself and the marsh gas is ignited by gunfire, setting Goth ablaze. The fight devolves into brutal hand-to-hand struggle in shallow water.
events: Doctor staggers through marsh and identifies marsh gas
Goth unmasks and confronts Doctor
Gunfire ignites gas, Goth catches fire and falls into water
Goth attempts to drown Doctor; Doctor strikes back and escapes as the Matrix collapses
